summary: Trickshot Cup phase 6: smoothness, game flow, menu flow and multiplayer correctness - 6 reviewers, 3 fixers, 1 verifier
logs: Review: 9 findings, 9 after dedup (1 blockers, 5 major)

findings.problem:
A LATE WAVE (design 10: "A leaver whose pending human-vs-human round became human-vs-AI hands the other human a late wave") is opened by `H2HStartWave(false)` -> `SetPhase(CupPhase.Loading)` (line 360) from call sites that run while `Phase` is ALREADY a wave phase. `HeadToHeadEnter` only clears the per-wave latch on a NON-wave entry:

    215: bool wave = phase == CupPhase.Loading || phase == CupPhase.CoinToss || phase == CupPhase.Round;
    219: if (!wave) _h2hWavePrepared = false;
    ...
    240: case CupPhase.Loading:
    241:     if (!_h2hWavePrepared) H2HPrepareWave();

`_h2hWavePrepared` is written in exactly two places (grep returns only 117, 219, 241, 246, 252, 373), so on a Round -> Loading edge it is still `true` from the previous wave and `H2HPrepareWave()` is SKIPPED on every peer. Three consequences, all at once:

(a) The owner of the late-wave round never calls `StartRound`. `H2HPrepareWave` (371-434) is the ONLY place `_h2hLocal` is set to `H2HLocal.Loading` and `_h2hRoundStarted` to false; with `_h2hLocal` still `Done` (set at line 627 by `H2HFinishLocalRound`) or `None`, `H2HTickLocalFlow`'s switch (line 561) matches nothing, so `H2HTickLoading` and `H2HTickRound` do nothing and the round is never played.

(b) Nobody re-acks the loading barrier. `H2HStartWave` calls `ClearLoaded()` (line 346), but `H2HSendLoaded` is latched by the stale `_h2hLoadedSent` (line 445 `if (_h2hLoadedSent) return;`), whose only reset is `H2HPrepareWave` line 376. So `AllLoaded` (CupDirector.cs:824) stays false and the host waits the full `CupTuning.LoadBarrierTimeout` (10 s) at line 465 before Loading -> Round.

(c) The wave then never completes on the normal path. `H2HWaveWatchdog` (854-887) only starts its `HeadToHeadResultGrace` clock for an owner it has SEEN Playing (`_h2hOwnerSeenPlaying.Add(owner)` at 869, gated on `p.Playing` at 867); since that peer never starts the round, `p.Playing` is never true and the grace path never arms. Only `capped` (857, `HeadToHeadWaveCap` = 480 s, line 91) settles it — eight minutes of a frozen cup, then the round is simulated out from under the player whose turn it was.

The three reachable wave-phase -> Loading edges are `H2HTickRound` line 548 (`H2HHostAdvance(true)` while Phase == Round), `H2HFinishHostRound` line 702 (`H2HHostAdvance(false)` while Phase == Round) and `H2HHostRoundUnplayable` line 742 (called from `H2HTickLoading` 458, `H2HTickCoinToss` 479, `H2HTickRound` 522) — each falls through `H2HHostAdvance` 777-783 `if (pending.Count > 0) { H2HStartWave(false); return; }`.
findings.fix: Reset the per-wave latches where a wave is OPENED instead of only on a non-wave phase entry. The narrowest correct form uses the serial that already exists: latch `_h2hWaveSerial = PhaseSerial` inside `H2HPrepareWave` (line 373) and test `_h2hWaveSerial != PhaseSerial` at lines 241 / 246 / 252 in place of `!_h2hWavePrepared`. `SetPhase` bumps `PhaseSerial` on every wave open and the host's serial rides `CupState` already (CupNet.BuildState sets `m.phaseSerial`, applied at CupDirector.Net.cs:520-524), so no new wire field and no `CupNet.StateVersion` / `NetCodec.ProtocolVersion` bump is needed. Side effect to preserve: lines 246 and 252 use the SAME latch to avoid re-preparing MID-wave, so `H2HPrepareWave` must re-latch on whichever of the three entries it actually runs from, and Loading -> CoinToss -> Round inside one wave must keep `_h2hHostRound` / `_h2hLocal` / `_h2hRoundStarted` untouched. All the fields are private to this partial and nothing outside `Assets/Scripts/Cup/` reads them.
findings.evidence:
CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:219 `if (!wave) _h2hWavePrepared = false;`; :241 `if (!_h2hWavePrepared) H2HPrepareWave();`; :373 `_h2hWavePrepared = true;`. :346 `ClearLoaded();` and :360 `SetPhase(CupPhase.Loading);` inside `H2HStartWave`. :445 `if (_h2hLoadedSent) return;` in `H2HSendLoaded`, reset only at :376. :548 `if (IsAuthority) H2HHostAdvance(true);`; :702 `H2HHostAdvance(false);`; :781 `H2HStartWave(false);`. :857 `bool capped = now - _h2hWaveStartedAt > HeadToHeadWaveCap;` with :91 `public const float HeadToHeadWaveCap = 480f;`; :867-877 the grace clock arms only after `p.Playing` was seen. CupDirector.cs:824-835 `AllLoaded` needs every Active player's `Loaded`; CupDirector.Net.cs:91 `LoadBarrierOpen => !IsNetworked || AllLoaded || PhaseTime >= CupTuning.LoadBarrierTimeout;`.

Call path: host A + clients B, C; draw A-vs-AI and B-vs-C. Bracket -> Loading is non-wave, so the latch clears and every peer prepares the first wave: A gets `_h2hLocal = Loading`, B and C have no round so `H2HPrepareWave` line 433 calls `H2HSendLoaded()` and `_h2hLoadedSent` sticks true. C leaves; `ApplyLeave` (CupDirector.cs:1322) calls `Bracket.MarkReplacedByAi`, and CupBracket.cs:28 `IsHuman => HumanSlot >= 0 && !ReplacedByAi` turns B-vs-C into a human-vs-AI round, so `H2HPendingParallelRounds` (902-913, `if (a != b) into.Add(r)`) now returns it. A's wave finishes -> `H2HTickRound` :548 -> `H2HHostAdvance(true)` -> :777 `pending.Count == 1` -> `H2HStartWave(false)` -> `SetPhase(Loading)` with Phase == Round. On A and on B that Loading entry is wave->wave, the latch is stale-true, `H2HPrepareWave` is skipped, B never `StartRound`s and never re-acks.

findings.symbol: EmotePose.Apply, case Celebration.Emote.TrophyLift (looped by CupPodium.Update and CupTrophyLift.Update)
findings.problem:
The champion's trophy arm drops to his hip and is re-raised every 2.5 seconds, for the whole podium and the whole Co-op trophy lift.

TrophyLift is a ONE-SHOT emote authored with a rise-from-rest ease-in, but both cup endings LOOP it as a held pose:

    float k = Mathf.SmoothStep(0f, 1f, Mathf.Clamp01(p / 0.35f));                    (Celebration.cs:892)
    float pump = Mathf.Sin(Mathf.Clamp01((p - 0.55f) / 0.2f) * Mathf.PI) * 14f * k;  (Celebration.cs:893)
    set(Bone.UpperArmL, new Vector3(-10f * k, 0f, (162f - pump) * k));               (Celebration.cs:895)

At p = 1 (the emote's last frame) k = 1 and pump = 0, so UpperArmL.z = 162 deg, arms fully overhead. At p = 0 on the very next play k = 0, so UpperArmL.z = 0, arms hanging at the sides. Solving the ramp: p=0 -> 0 deg; p=0.10 (0.25 s) -> 32 deg; p=0.175 (0.44 s) -> 81 deg; p=0.25 (0.62 s) -> 130 deg; p=0.35 (0.88 s) -> 162 deg. Duration is 2.5 s (Celebration.cs:204), so the arms sit below the raised pose for 0.88 s of every 2.5 s, a 35% duty cycle.

The trophy is a Cosmetics.Piece parented to Bone.ForearmL (CupTrophy.AttachToHand, CupTrophy.cs:150-167), a 0.45 m gold cup, so the whole trophy swings down past the champion's head to his hip and back up on every loop.

CALL PATHS, both reached in normal play:

1. Podium (Solo and Head to Head, design 8.1):
     CupPodium.Update -> "if (HandedOver && Winner.Celeb != null && !Winner.Celeb.Playing) Winner.Celeb.Play(Celebration.Emote.TrophyLift);" (CupPodium.cs:540)
   Podium.LateUpdate holds a pose sized for exactly this arm position - "HoldUpperArmL = new Vector3(-10f, 0f, 165f)" (CupPodium.cs:79), three degrees off TrophyLift's own 162 - but applies it only under "if (celeb != null && celeb.Playing && celeb.CurrentEmote != Celebration.Emote.TrophyLift)" (CupPodium.cs:563), i.e. ONLY while a DIFFERENT wheel emote plays. It covers Wave/Salute/Point/Thinker and covers nothing while TrophyLift itself ramps. The podium also has a one-frame hole: Celebration.End does "_ragdoll.ClearPoseOverrides()" and sets _playing = false (Celebration.cs:250-253), so on a frame where Celebration.Update runs after CupPodium.Update the podium's LateUpdate sees celeb.Playing == false, fails the line-563 test, and leaves the arm with no override at all. Neither type declares [DefaultExecutionOrder] and there is no execution-order asset in ProjectSettings, so that ordering is genuinely undefined.

2. Co-op trophy lift (design 8.2):
     CupTrophyLift.Update -> "if (Captain != null && Captain.Alive && Captain.Celeb != null && !Captain.Celeb.Playing) PlayLift();" (CupTrophyLift.cs:404); PlayLift -> Celeb.Play(TrophyLift) (CupTrophyLift.cs:358).
   Its LateUpdate hold is inverted relative to the podium's - "bool lifting = c != null && c.Playing && c.CurrentEmote == Celebration.Emote.TrophyLift; if (!lifting) { SetPoseOverride(UpperArmL, CupPodium.HoldUpperArmL); ... }" (CupTrophyLift.cs:438-442) - so it DOES cover the between-plays hole, but explicitly stands down while TrophyLift plays, which is exactly the 0.88 s ramp. Same drop.

Visible on every peer. On the authority the pose is a joint-drive target, so the arm swings down under the solver. On a client the champion is a puppet and ActiveRagdoll.DisplayEmote calls the SAME formula - "EmotePose.Apply(e, pc, (bone, euler) => over[(int)bone] = euler);" (ActiveRagdoll.cs:1626) - then writes bone transforms directly (ActiveRagdoll.cs:1643), so a client sees the arm and trophy TELEPORT down and back rather than swing.

Why it survived review: the Celebration comment asserts the opposite - "the arms rise over the first 0.35 of the emote, then hold with a slow sway and one small pump ... so a lift re-played every 2.5 s reads as a celebration, never a statue" (Celebration.cs:882-884). The sway and pump do provide the life; the ramp-from-zero on every re-play is the part nobody solved for. CupPodium's own header documents the loop as intended ("TrophyLift re-played whenever it drops", CupPodium.cs:11) without noticing what p=0 does to the arm.
findings.fix:
Make the rise happen ONCE, not on every re-play, by extending the two hold paths that already exist rather than by touching the shared emote.

In both loopers, apply the hold pose whenever the arm is not already at full height, not only when a foreign emote plays:
  - CupPodium.cs:563 - replace
      if (celeb != null && celeb.Playing && celeb.CurrentEmote != Celebration.Emote.TrophyLift)
    with the CupTrophyLift form plus a ramp test:
      bool lifting = celeb != null && celeb.Playing && celeb.CurrentEmote == Celebration.Emote.TrophyLift;
      if (!lifting || celeb.Progress01 < 0.35f)
    (Celebration.Progress01 is already public - cup-build-notes lists it beside Playing/CurrentEmote.)
  - CupTrophyLift.cs:438 - add the same term to its existing !lifting:
      if (!lifting || (c != null && c.Progress01 < 0.35f))

That pins UpperArmL/ForearmL to HoldUpperArmL for the whole 0.88 s window the emote would otherwise spend below it, and lets the emote own the arm for the sway-and-pump section it was authored for. The right arm, torso and head keep their full ramp, which is harmless since they start and end near rest.

SIDE EFFECTS, stated explicitly:
  - Do NOT fix this by editing the k formula at Celebration.cs:892 (e.g. dropping the p/0.35 ramp). EmotePose.Apply is the shared formula used by the live Celebration AND by ActiveRagdoll.DisplayEmote for every networked puppet, and the same switch carries all 38 emotes. Changing the emote's own shape also changes the FIRST lift, and both CupPodium.HandOver (CupPodium.cs:576-582) and CupTrophyLift's CueHandOver want a body that visibly RAISES the trophy on the cut - which the ramp exists to give. The bug is the loop, not the ramp.
  - The two edits above touch only CupPodium.cs and CupTrophyLift.cs. Celebration.cs, EmotePose, the wire id (TrophyLift = 33) and every other mode are untouched; grep confirms TrophyLift has no consumer outside those two files.
  - HoldUpperArmL is 165 while TrophyLift's peak is 162, a 3 deg step at the hand-off. Consider making them equal (either value) so the transition into and out of the hold is exactly continuous.
  - The podium's one-frame hole is only reachable because line 563 keys off celeb.Playing; adopting the !lifting form closes it as a by-product, which is why matching CupTrophyLift's shape is the better edit than adding a separate gap guard.

findings.problem: During a Head to Head PARALLEL wave, the host's own live row is written every tick without ever firing StateChanged, so it is never broadcast. UpdateLiveRow() (CupDirector.cs:1727-1734) ends with `me.SetLive(Bracket.Entrants[CurrentRound.OpponentOf(me.Entrant)].NationIndex, own, theirs, Driver.KickIndex + 1);` and NO Notify(). Its sibling for a REMOTE player, ApplyLiveRow (CupDirector.Net.cs:241-249), does call Notify() — that asymmetry is the bug. In the parallel wave the host's per-tick path is H2HTickRound -> H2HTickLocalFlow() case H2HLocal.Playing: -> UpdateLiveRow(); (CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:598-601), then H2HHostAdvance(true), whose only Notify calls are inside H2HResolveParallelCalls() (`if (changed) Notify();`, line 1031 — nothing changes mid-round) and the watchdog's sim path. I grepped every Notify() in CupDirector.cs and CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs: none sits on the per-kick or per-tick path of a host-owned parallel round. So the only CupState carrying the host's row is the one from StartRound's `me.SetLive(..., 0, 0, 1); Notify();` (CupDirector.cs:1720-1722). The in-code comment at HeadToHead.cs:600 ("a client's row reaches the host through CupRequest.LiveRow (automatic)") accounts for the inbound direction only. This is NOT the host-round case: there H2HSetHostRoundLive (HeadToHead.cs:658-678) calls ApplyLiveRow for the remote participant, whose Notify() incidentally flushes the host's row too.
findings.fix: Make UpdateLiveRow() notify on change, the way ApplyLiveRow does: in CupDirector.cs:1727 snapshot the four fields before SetLive and call Notify() only when one of (LiveOpponentNation, LiveScoreFor, LiveScoreAgainst, LiveKick, Playing) actually moved. An UNCONDITIONAL Notify() there would be wrong — it would fire StateChanged every frame of every round, and although NetFlushState coalesces to 10/s (CupNet.StateCoalesceSeconds) it would still rebuild and send a ~700 B reliable CupState ten times a second for the whole round, and NetOnStateChanged walks every player twice and writes SetCupSpectating per player on each fire. SIDE EFFECT: UpdateLiveRow is shared by all three styles — CupDirector.Solo.cs:117, CupDirector.Coop.cs:487 and both Head-to-Head call sites — so the change-gated Notify also starts firing in Solo (harmless: StateChanged has no host subscriber there, NetBind only hooks it when _netHost) and in Co-op (where it is equally correct: the Co-op host's row is just as stale today, though Co-op has no lobby drawing it).
findings.evidence: CupDirector.cs:1726-1734 `public void UpdateLiveRow() { var me = LocalPlayer; if (me == null || Driver == null || CurrentRound == null || me.Entrant < 0 || !CurrentRound.Involves(me.Entrant)) return; ... me.SetLive(Bracket.Entrants[CurrentRound.OpponentOf(me.Entrant)].NationIndex, own, theirs, Driver.KickIndex + 1); }` — no Notify. Contrast CupDirector.Net.cs:245-248 `if (playing) p.SetLive(opponentNation, scoreFor, scoreAgainst, kick); else p.ClearLive(); Notify();`. Caller: CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:598-601 `case H2HLocal.Playing: if (Driver == null) { H2HLocalUnplayable(); return; } UpdateLiveRow();   // a client's row reaches the host through CupRequest.LiveRow (automatic)`. Consumers of the stale row on a client: CupSpectatorView.cs:272-273 `string sub = p.Playing ? "KICK " + Mathf.Max(1, p.LiveKick) : ""; Hud.Scoreboard(home, homeCol, p.LiveScoreFor, p.LiveScoreAgainst, away, awayCol, -1f, false, sub);` and CupLobbyUI.cs:326 `return CupText.StatusPlaying(opp, p.LiveScoreFor, p.LiveScoreAgainst, Mathf.Max(1, p.LiveKick));`. Failure path: 3+ humans at the Round of 32, the host drawn against an AI and at least one other human also drawn against an AI, so both play parallel rounds. A third human (or any human whose own round finished first) presses Spectate on the host's row — CupSpectatorView opens, _d.Driver is null so its OnGUI branch runs (CupSpectatorView.cs:262), and it draws `Hud.Scoreboard(..., 0, 0, ..., "KICK 1")` over the streamed puppets for the host's entire five-kick round while goals visibly go in. The lobby row for the host reads "Playing vs GHA - 0-0 - kick 1" for the same duration. p.Playing itself is correct (set by the StartRound Notify), so Spectate works — only the numbers are frozen.

findings.fix: Have `UpdateLiveRow` fire `Notify()` when it actually changed something — snapshot the previous `Playing` / `LiveOpponentNation` / `LiveScoreFor` / `LiveScoreAgainst` / `LiveKick` and Notify only on a difference, so a per-frame call does not mark the state dirty 60 times a second (the coalescer at `CupNet.StateCoalesceSeconds` = 0.1 s caps the wire at 10/s, but a per-frame dirty flag also wakes `NetOnStateChanged`'s two O(players) loops every frame). Side effect: `UpdateLiveRow` is called from all four sites (Solo.cs:117, HeadToHead.cs:600 and :663, Coop.cs:487) and `Notify()` raises `StateChanged`, to which `CupResultsUI` (line 67) and `CupLobbyUI` are subscribed — change-gating keeps that at the rate the model actually moves (once a kick), so those screens see no extra load, and Solo has no listener that cares. `EndRound`'s `me.ClearLive()` (CupDirector.cs:1755) is silent in the same way but is always followed by a Notify from `RecordResult`, so it needs no change.

findings.fix:
Pass touchCursor: false on the Over/Idle edge — the driver already owns the cursor for that transition and has just set it correctly:

  if ((phase == RoundPhase.Over || phase == RoundPhase.Idle) && _wheelOpen) SetWheel(false, false);

That still clears _wheelOpen and still pushes `_driver.EmoteWheelOpen = false` (CupHud.cs:279), which is all the Over edge needs. It matches the file's own precedent two lines up at CupHud.cs:173 and :184, where the wheel is closed with touchCursor: false precisely because someone else owns the cursor at that moment.

SIDE EFFECT: none outside CupHud — SetWheel is private and CupEmoteWheel.SetOpen is unchanged, so CupPodium/CupTrophyLift keep their behaviour.

SEVERITY NOTE, stated honestly: I could not turn this into a permanently stuck cursor. Every screen that follows calls GameInput.CaptureCursor(false) in its Init (CupLobbyUI.cs:103, CupKnockedOutUI.cs:61, CupResultsUI.cs:329, CupBracketScreen.cs:64, CupPodium.cs:240), and in Head to Head the lobby is genuinely re-created after a round rather than reused (CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:424 CloseLobby() before the wave, :628 EnsureLobby() after H2HFinishLocalRound). So the observable symptom is a locked cursor for the frame or two between Over and the next screen's Init, plus a mouse-look kick on the camera during it. Worth fixing because the ordering is plainly wrong and a future flow that reuses a screen instead of recreating it would make it permanent — not worth calling a blocker.
findings.evidence: The trigger state is normal play, not an edge case. The wheel opens only while LocalFreed (CupHud.cs:200 `if (freed && _input != null && _input.EmotePressed) SetWheel(!_wheelOpen, true);`), and LocalFreed (CupHud.cs:452-468) is true during the scored window for the scorer and during the win beat for the winning side — i.e. the celebration windows the design tells the player to emote in (design 2.7: "Won the round: whole lineup free to move and emote | 5 s"). The win beat ends into RoundPhase.Decided and then straight to Over: CupRoundDriver.Kick.cs:1051-1057 `if (PhaseTime >= _decidedSeconds || _skipRequested) { ... if (_replayPending) StartReplay(); else SetPhase(RoundPhase.Over); }`. A player still holding the wheel open when that 5 s expires hits this every time. The other Over path, Abort (CupRoundDriver.cs:305), calls OnAbort -> EndRoundVisuals at Kick.cs:140 BEFORE `SetPhase(RoundPhase.Over)`, so it inverts the same way.

findings.problem: In the FREE KICKS format the cup allocates a DefensiveWall per ROUND, and each wall leaks one PhysicsMaterial that nothing ever destroys. CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:393 `_wall = new DefensiveWall();` sits inside BuildScene, which runs from `partial void OnConfigured()` (CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:339) - i.e. once per CupDirector.StartRound, per round. DefensiveWall lazily creates its blocker physics material on the first build: `if (_bounce == null) _bounce = Make.PhysMat("WallBlocker", 0.45f, 0.4f, 0.4f);` (DefensiveWall.cs:100-101), where `Make.PhysMat` is `var pm = new PhysicsMaterial(name)` (Make.cs:432) - a Unity Object, so it is not collected without an explicit Destroy. `DefensiveWall.Clear()` (DefensiveWall.cs:247-257) destroys `_blockers` and the three `_mats` entries but never touches `_bounce`, and `_bounce` is not in the `Track(...)`-ed `_mats` list (only the shirt/shorts/skin materials are, DefensiveWall.cs:112-114). DefensiveWall is a plain class with no OnDestroy. The cup's own teardown, `partial void OnTornDown()` at CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:430, does `if (_wall != null) { _wall.Clear(); _wall = null; }` - which is the documented contract, and it is still not enough for `_bounce`. I grepped for any disposal: `grep -rn "Destroy(_bounce\|Destroy(.*PhysMat\|Destroy(.*physMat" Assets/Scripts/` returns nothing; nothing in the repo destroys a PhysicsMaterial. This is latent in the shared file rather than new, but the cup is the first caller that makes it compound: `grep -rn "new DefensiveWall()" Assets/Scripts/` gives four sites, and the other three are once-per-MATCH (GameBootstrap.cs:1099 in BuildFreeKickMode, NetSetPieceMatch.cs:250 in Configure, FreeKickScene.cs:38 in a menu vignette), so they leak one object for a whole session. The cup leaks one per round: up to 5 for a Solo run to the Final, times again for every Play Again in the same process (design 9.5 keeps one process across cups), and in Head to Head a non-participating peer also builds a Client-authority driver per wave to watch through, so a spectator accumulates them at the same rate.
findings.fix: Free it where the other wall materials are freed: in DefensiveWall.Clear(), after the `_mats` loop, add `if (_bounce != null) { Object.Destroy(_bounce); _bounce = null; }`. The lazy `if (_bounce == null)` guard at DefensiveWall.cs:100 already re-creates it on the next BuildAt, so a Clear-then-rebuild (which is exactly what CupRoundDriver.RebuildWallFor drives via BuildAt's own leading `Clear()`) still works. SIDE EFFECT - this edits a SHARED file: DefensiveWall is also used by single-player free kicks (GameBootstrap.BuildFreeKickMode), networked set pieces (NetSetPieceMatch) and the FreeKickScene menu vignette. Those three call Clear() only on teardown/rebuild, so the change is behaviour-neutral for them (they get the same material re-created on the next build), but it does mean the material is now destroyed on every rebuild rather than reused - a per-pair allocation in the cup instead of a per-round one, which is cheaper than the leak but not free. If that churn is unwanted, the alternative is to leave Clear() alone and add an explicit `Dispose()`/`Free()` to DefensiveWall that Clear()s AND destroys `_bounce`, then call that from CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:430 instead of `_wall.Clear()` - which confines the change to the cup at the cost of the other three call sites keeping their (bounded, one-per-match) leak. I did not edit any code; this is a report only.

findings.problem: CupStateMsg.leverPulls is a byte and CupNet.BuildState saturates the director's int at 255: `m.leverPulls = (byte)Mathf.Clamp(d.LeverPulls, 0, 255);` (CupNet.cs:55). CupDirector.RollOrder increments LeverPulls on every pull with no cap (CupDirector.cs:1290-1293) and it is only reset per stage by ClearOrder. Clients detect a pull purely by the value CHANGING — CupOrderUI.cs:142-146 `int pulls = _director.LeverPulls; if (pulls != _pullsSeen) { if (pulls > 0) StartReel(); _pullsSeen = pulls; }` and CupDirector.Coop.cs:641-644 `int pulls = LeverPulls; if (pulls == _coopLeverSeen) return;` — so from the 256th pull of a stage onward the value is stuck at 255 on every client and the slot-machine reels stop animating for them. The new order still arrives (it rides CupState.order), so nothing desyncs; only the animation is lost, and only for clients (the host reads its own un-clamped int). Separately, RollOrder's salt `CupSalts.Order(Stage) + 16u * (uint)LeverPulls` (CupDirector.cs:1290) reaches 0x6000 + 4096 = 0x7000 at 256 pulls on stage 0, which is exactly CupSalts.Podium (CupTypes.cs:138) — a real overlap of the salt space, though harmless in effect since the two streams have independent consumers.
findings.fix: Cap the pull counter where it is incremented rather than where it is sent: in CupDirector.cs:1292 use `LeverPulls = (LeverPulls + 1) & 0xFF;` to fix the wire saturation, and mask the pull count to fewer bits before the 16x (or use a smaller multiplier) so the salt stays inside the 0x6000 family. SIDE EFFECT: none outside the cup — LeverPulls and CupSalts.Order have no callers other than CupDirector.RollOrder, CupOrderUI and CupDirector.Coop.CoopWatchLever (verified by grep across Assets/Scripts). But changing the salt arithmetic DOES change which permutation a given (seed, stage, pull) produces, so it must land on every peer at once; it is not wire-compatible with an unpatched build mid-cup.
findings.evidence: CupNet.cs:55 `m.leverPulls = (byte)Mathf.Clamp(d.LeverPulls, 0, 255);`. CupDirector.cs:1288-1293 `var rng = new SeededRng(Seed).Fork(CupSalts.Order(Stage) + 16u * (uint)LeverPulls); rng.Shuffle(team); LeverPulls++; return ApplyOrder(team.ToArray());`. CupDirector.Net.cs:508 `LeverPulls = m.leverPulls;` — the client takes the clamped byte. CupOrderUI.cs:142-146 and CupDirector.Coop.cs:641-644 both branch only on a CHANGE of that value. CupTypes.cs:138 `public const uint Podium = 0x7000u;` vs CupTypes.cs:147 `const uint OrderFamily = 0x6000u;` — 0x6000 + 0 + 16*256 == 0x7000.

=== h2h-late-wave-never-prepared (blocker) — FIXED, but NOT with the proposed fix ===

VERIFIED. `grep -rn "h2hWavePrepared" Assets/` returns exactly the six lines the finding names (117 decl, 219 clear, 241/246/252 test, 373 set) — no other writer. Confirmed `SetPhase(CupPhase.Loading)` in the H2H flow exists at exactly two sites, CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:360 (H2HStartWave) and :1083 (H2HTickInterstitial), and both are wave OPENS. Confirmed the Round->Loading edge: H2HTickRound:548 `if (IsAuthority) H2HHostAdvance(true);` -> :781 `H2HStartWave(false);` -> :360 `SetPhase(CupPhase.Loading);` while Phase is still Round, so `wave` is true at :215 and the latch is not cleared. Confirmed a CLIENT re-enters the same way: CupDirector.Net.cs:520-523 `if (m.phaseSerial != _lastPhaseSerial) { ...; SetPhase(phase, m.phaseTime); }` bumps the local PhaseSerial (CupDirector.cs:623), so `_h2hSerial != PhaseSerial` fires HeadToHeadEnter(Loading) with the same stale latch. Consequences (a)/(b)/(c) all check out: `_h2hLoadedSent` (:445) is reset only at :376, and H2HWaveWatchdog:867-877 arms its grace clock only after `p.Playing` was seen.

I DID NOT USE THE PROPOSED FIX. Latching `_h2hWaveSerial = PhaseSerial` in H2HPrepareWave and testing `_h2hWaveSerial != PhaseSerial` at 241/246/252 would REGRESS the host-round path: a wave is Loading -> CoinToss -> Round, and each of those is its own SetPhase, so PhaseSerial is bumped between them. On the CoinToss entry (:246) the serial would no longer match and H2HPrepareWave would run a SECOND time MID-wave, blowing away `_h2hHostRound`, `_h2hRoundStarted`, `_h2hLoadedSent`, `_h2hTossDone` and `_h2hLocal` on the peer and re-issuing StartRound/Spectate. That is precisely the "side effect to preserve" the finding itself warns about, and re-latching inside H2HPrepareWave does not avoid it (the serial has already moved). The reviewer's DIAGNOSIS is correct; their prescribed mechanism is not.

WHAT I DID instead (CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:219, one term added):
  if (!wave || phase == CupPhase.Loading) _h2hWavePrepared = false;
A Loading entry always opens a wave (both SetPhase(Loading) call sites, verified by grep), and CoinToss / Round are only ever entered mid-wave, so they keep the latch and cannot re-prepare. This is the narrowest change that covers all three reachable wave-phase -> Loading edges (:548, :702, :742 -> :781) plus the client's mirrored entry, with no new field, no wire change and no CupNet.StateVersion / NetCodec.ProtocolVersion bump.

Re-prepare safety checked on the late-wave edge: the peer that just finished ran H2HFinishLocalRound -> EndRound(), and CupDirector.cs:1764-1765 sets `Driver = null; CurrentRound = null;`, so `HostRound` (CupDirector.Net.cs:83 `IsAuthority ? CurrentRound : _hostRound`) is null on the host and, via CupNet's `m.currentRound` applied at CupDirector.Net.cs:511 BEFORE the SetPhase at :522, null on clients too. So H2HPrepareWave takes the non-host-round branch correctly. A peer already mid-round when a wave re-opens is still protected by the existing :416-423 "already playing it" branch. The host-round path (Interstitial -> Loading) is unchanged: that entry came from a NON-wave phase, so the latch was already being cleared there.

SIDE EFFECTS: none outside Assets/Scripts/Cup/. `_h2hWavePrepared` is private to this partial and has no other reader (grep above). Solo and Co-op have no equivalent latch (`grep -n "Prepared" CupDirector.Coop.cs` returns nothing).

=== cup-h2h-watchbar-paused-early-return (major) — FIXED as proposed ===

VERIFIED. PauseMenu.cs:410 `if (hit) { Activate(_entries[i]); break; }` sits inside the menu's OnGUI draw; PauseMenu.cs:248-258 `Activate` invokes `e.Act`, and PauseMenu.cs:269 registers the Resume entry as `Act = Resume`, whose body at :212 is `Paused = false`. Checked their stability: their length depends on `e.IsHuman`, which only changes via `Bracket.MarkReplacedByAi` (CupBracket.cs:667), called from CupDirector.cs:1322 (ApplyLeave) and CupDirector.Net.cs:627 — both on the net tick, never inside a GUI pass. Moving them to a latched model is a cleanup, not a correctness fix, so I did not do it (smallest correct change).

=== cup-hud-recaptures-cursor-at-round-over (minor) — FIXED as proposed ===

VERIFIED, and the ordering is exactly as described. CupRoundDriver.cs:362-363 calls `OnPhaseChanged(prev, next);` and only THEN `PhaseChanged?.Invoke(next);`. OnPhaseChanged reaches CupRoundDriver.Kick.cs:249-250 `case RoundPhase.Over: EndRoundVisuals(); break;` -> Kick.cs:1075 `if (_cursorCaptured) { GameInput.CaptureCursor(false); _cursorCaptured = false; }`. PhaseChanged then reaches CupHud.OnPhase -> SetWheel(false, true) -> CupEmoteWheel.cs:64-69 `GameInput.CaptureCursor(!value)` with value false, i.e. CaptureCursor(TRUE). The HUD wins.

Also confirmed `_cursorCaptured` is genuinely true at that moment: it is set at Kick.cs:128 on Begin for a local-body player, and opening the wheel frees the cursor via CupEmoteWheel.SetOpen WITHOUT touching that flag (grep: the only writers are Kick.cs:128/1075/1297/1320 and Scene.cs:449), so EndRoundVisuals really does fire its release on this edge.

I left it alone; it is a harmless belt-and-braces term and removing it is out of scope.

fixes.notes:
VERIFICATION OF cup-net-1 / h2h-host-live-row-never-broadcast (the same defect, reported twice)

Both findings are CONFIRMED. Every load-bearing claim checked:

1. The write with no Notify. CupDirector.cs:1727-1735 (pre-edit) ended `me.SetLive(Bracket.Entrants[CurrentRound.OpponentOf(me.Entrant)].NationIndex, own, theirs, Driver.KickIndex + 1);` and the method body contained no `Notify()`. Its sibling CupDirector.Net.cs:241-249 `ApplyLiveRow` does: `if (playing) p.SetLive(opponentNation, scoreFor, scoreAgainst, kick); else p.ClearLive(); Notify();` — the asymmetry is exactly as described.

2. Notify is the only thing that dirties the wire. CupDirector.cs:628-632 `public void Notify() { StateChanged?.Invoke(); }` is the sole raiser. CupDirector.Net.cs:283 `_stateDirty = true;` sits only inside `NetOnStateChanged`, subscribed at :136 `StateChanged += NetOnStateChanged;` under `if (_netHost)`. CupDirector.Net.cs:290 `if (!_stateDirty && !force && !_stateForce) return;` in NetFlushState — I read the whole method and there is no periodic/heartbeat resend.

3. The host's parallel-wave tick genuinely never Notifies. Traced H2HTickRound (HeadToHead.cs:516) -> the non-`_h2hHostRound` branch at :546-549 `H2HTickLocalFlow(); if (IsAuthority) H2HHostAdvance(true); H2HLobbyBackdrop();`. H2HTickLocalFlow's `case H2HLocal.Playing:` (:598-601) calls only `UpdateLiveRow()` then tests `Driver.Phase`. H2HHostAdvance (:757-767) calls `SimulateAiRounds(Stage)` and `H2HResolveParallelCalls()`; the latter's only Notify is `if (changed) Notify();` at :1031, gated on a coin-call verdict landing (`p.CoinCall.HasValue && !p.CoinCallRight.HasValue && r.Done`) — nothing that moves mid-round. I grepped every `Notify()` in CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs (lines 620, 647, 692, 737, 797, 885, 980, 1031) and none is on the per-kick or per-tick path of a host-owned parallel round.

4. The client is genuinely unaffected. NetTickLiveRow (CupDirector.Net.cs:726-743) polls `me.Playing`/`me.LiveScoreFor`/... off the model directly and sends CupRequest.LiveRow, whose host handler ApplyLiveRow Notifies. So the fix is only needed for the host — but it is needed there.

5. The consumers of the stale row are as quoted. CupLobbyUI.cs:302 `bool canSpectate = h2h && !isMe && p.Active && p.Playing;` with the button parked off-screen at :304 when `!show`; CupLobbyUI.cs:322-327 `if (p.Playing) { ... return CupText.StatusPlaying(opp, p.LiveScoreFor, p.LiveScoreAgainst, Mathf.Max(1, p.LiveKick)); }` vs the "Up next vs XXX" fallthrough at :356-361.

One correction to the reports: cup-net-1 says Spectate still works and only the numbers freeze; h2h-host-live-row-never-broadcast says Playing is false on clients and Spectate is unreachable. The SECOND is right for the parallel case. StartRound (CupDirector.cs:1719-1722) does `me.SetLive(..., 0, 0, 1); Notify();` — but on a client that Notify only reaches the client's own model; the host's Notify there DOES broadcast, so clients do see `Playing == true` with 0-0 kick 1. So cup-net-1's account of the symptom is the accurate one, and the practical effect is the frozen 0-0/kick-1 row plus a spectator scoreboard that never moves. Either way the fix is the same and it is worth making.

THE FIX APPLIED (CupDirector.cs:1726-1751)

Change-gated Notify, as both reports prescribe:

    int opp = Bracket.Entrants[CurrentRound.OpponentOf(me.Entrant)].NationIndex;
    int kick = Driver.KickIndex + 1;
    bool changed = !me.Playing || me.LiveOpponentNation != opp || me.LiveScoreFor != own
                || me.LiveScoreAgainst != theirs || me.LiveKick != kick;
    me.SetLive(opp, own, theirs, kick);
    if (changed) Notify();

`!me.Playing` is included in the change test because SetLive sets `Playing = true` (CupDirector.cs:158-165), so a row coming back from ClearLive must count as a change even when the four numbers happen to match. The Notify fires AFTER SetLive so a subscriber reads the new values.

Re-entrancy checked before committing to this: `grep -rn "StateChanged +=" Assets/Scripts/` returns exactly two subscribers — CupDirector.Net.cs:136 `NetOnStateChanged` (two per-player loops + `_stateDirty = true` + a conditional NetFlushState) and CupResultsUI.cs:67 `OnState`. Neither re-enters UpdateLiveRow, so the added Notify cannot recurse.

SIDE EFFECTS, as flagged in the reports and confirmed by grep. UpdateLiveRow has four call sites — CupDirector.Solo.cs:117, CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:600, CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs:663 (inside H2HSetHostRoundLive) and CupDirector.Coop.cs:487 — and all four now Notify once per kick instead of never:
- Solo: NetBind only hooks NetOnStateChanged when `_netHost`, and Solo is not networked, so the only listener is CupResultsUI.OnState. Harmless.
- Co-op: correct for the same reason it is correct in H2H (the Co-op host's row was equally stale), and Co-op has no lobby drawing it, so no visible change.
- H2H host round (HeadToHead.cs:658-678): H2HSetHostRoundLive already called ApplyLiveRow for the remote participant, which Notified and incidentally flushed the host's row. That path now Notifies at most one extra time per kick — the coalescer at CupNet.StateCoalesceSeconds absorbs it, and note ApplyLiveRow there is itself already guarded by the `if (p.Playing && ... ) continue;` change test at :671, so this is the same discipline.
The wire cost is bounded by the model's real movement (once per kick), not by frame rate, which is why the unconditional Notify both reports warned against was avoided.

WHY CUP-MP-01 WAS SKIPPED (the finding is real; the fix is not in my files)

I verified every claim in it and found no error:
- Assets/Scripts/Cup/CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:392-396 `if (s.Format == CupFormat.FreeKicks) { _wall = new DefensiveWall(); RebuildWallFor(CupRoundRules.PairIndex(Line), spot); }` inside BuildScene, reached from `partial void OnConfigured()` at :339 — once per StartRound, i.e. per round.
- Assets/Scripts/Play/DefensiveWall.cs:28 `PhysicsMaterial _bounce;` and :100-101 `if (_bounce == null) _bounce = Make.PhysMat("WallBlocker", 0.45f, 0.4f, 0.4f);`.
- Assets/Scripts/Play/DefensiveWall.cs:247-257 Clear() destroys `_blockers` and the `_mats` entries and never touches `_bounce`; :243 `Material Track(Material m) { if (m != null) _mats.Add(m); return m; }` takes only the three kit Materials at :112-114, and `_bounce` is a PhysicsMaterial that could not go in a `List<Material>` anyway.
- Assets/Scripts/Cup/CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:430 `if (_wall != null) { _wall.Clear(); _wall = null; }` — the documented contract, and still not enough.
- `grep -rn "Destroy(_bounce\|Destroy(.*PhysMat\|Destroy(.*physMat" Assets/Scripts/` → no matches. Nothing in the repo destroys a PhysicsMaterial.

The blocker is access. `_bounce` is a PRIVATE field of DefensiveWall (DefensiveWall.cs:28) and the class's entire public surface is `Blockers`, `HasBlockers`, three `Build*` overloads, `TriggerJump`, `Tick`, `Ground`, `Clear` (grepped the public/internal members of the file). There is no Dispose, no Free, and no accessor that reaches `_bounce`. So:
- The reviewer's primary fix (add the destroy inside `DefensiveWall.Clear()`) needs Assets/Scripts/Play/DefensiveWall.cs.
- The reviewer's own "confined" alternative (add a `Dispose()`/`Free()` to DefensiveWall and call it from CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs:430) ALSO needs Assets/Scripts/Play/DefensiveWall.cs, since the new method has to live on that class to see the private field. It is confined in its BEHAVIOURAL blast radius, not in its file list.
Neither is writable from CupDirector.cs or CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs. FILE NEEDED: Assets/Scripts/Play/DefensiveWall.cs.

For whoever picks it up: the primary fix (inside Clear) is the better one and is behaviour-neutral for the three non-cup callers (GameBootstrap.cs:1099 BuildFreeKickMode, NetSetPieceMatch.cs:250 Configure, FreeKickScene.cs:38), because the lazy `if (_bounce == null)` guard at DefensiveWall.cs:100 re-creates it on the next BuildAt and every Build* overload leads with its own `Clear()`. The only cost is that the material is re-allocated per wall rebuild (in the cup, per free-kick PAIR via RebuildWallFor) rather than reused — one small PhysicsMaterial, far cheaper than the leak. Note that this makes it a shared-file edit affecting SP free kicks, networked set pieces and the FreeKickScene menu vignette, so it should be stated as such in the commit.

FILES NOT EDITED
Assets/Scripts/Cup/CupRoundDriver.Scene.cs — I own it, but the only finding against it (CUP-MP-01) could not be fixed from inside it, and I made no speculative changes.

BUILD STATE
`bash docs/compile-check.sh` → `exit=0` both immediately after the edit and again at the end (the second run also covered the parallel fixer's concurrent edits to CupCoinToss.cs, CupDirector.HeadToHead.cs, CupPenaltyCam.cs and CupTypes.cs, which were present in the tree and compiled clean alongside mine). CupDirector.cs re-checked as CRLF after normalisation. Nothing committed.
